notes.title: RICO DLC: Breakout is out now!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29255966/cd2c93b45836b28bc61268d42def73e1aa212fd3.png[/img]


In RICO: Breakout players must battle against a dangerous and unpredictable set of enemies that broke out of the San Amaro prison, bringing chaos to the area. With a city-wide curfew in place, it’s up to the RICO team to bring peace and order back to the city. RICO: Breakout introduces a brand-new environment with a set of new and highly effective weapons for players to use.

Grab the DLC here:   http://bit.ly/RICODLC

RICO: Breakout DLC Features

[u]·         New Weapons[/u]
o   G-18 - Fully automatic pistol
o   USG45 - High calibre submachine gun
o   K36 - Short-barrel special forces rifle

[u]·         New Level[/u]
o   A new lockdown level sees the player trapped in the San Amaro prison facing down the escaped prisoners trying to take them out.

[u]New In-game Soundtrack[/u]
Launching alongside the new Breakout DLC is a free update that introduces a highly requested in-game soundtrack for RICO. Players will experience seven brand-new music tracks that will underscore the game’s intense action.

notes.title: RICO Autumn Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29255966/2c6f21f4af6044ac62ab87024a9a39847077601e.png[/img]

The latest update for RICO adds two brand new modes, and fixes several issues that players have been experiencing with the game:

[b]Hardcore Case Mode[/b]
Players now have access to a brand new variation on case mode. Hardcore case allows players to take their existing selection of unlocked weapons and equipment into a new case, but at a higher difficulty level affording them the ultimate RICO challenge.

[b]Challenge Mode[/b]
Challenge mode is a whole new way to play RICO, with 27 levels (18 single player and 9 co-op) of intense goal-based action. Players will work against the clock to beat specific timed challenged within each level, pushing themselves and their skills to the limits.
Challenge mode also allows players to earn Reputation Points (RP) and unlock weapons skins in offline play for the very first time.
Changes and Fixes

-    Easier bomb defusal
-    Now easier to shoot enemies on stairs
-    Other small bug fixes

notes.title: Learn about the making of Disco Elysium, Observation and more at EGX on October 18th
notes.content:
Do you like hearing indie devs spilling the beans about the secrets of game design? Would you also like to see the lovely faces of RPS coaxing said developers to spill those beans at the same time? Well then, you better get yourself over to the Rezzed Sessions stage on Friday October 18th at EGX 2019, as we’ll be hogging the stage from 2.30pm onwards as we grill some friendly developers that just happened to walk into our big indie dev net. From the making of NoCode’s space horror game Observation to how to make an RPG like Disco Elysium, here’s the line-up for the second day of EGX 2019, which runs October 17th-20th at London’s ExCeL.

notes.title: Unknown Pleasures: Adventurer Time
notes.content:
Happy New Freelance Year! The receipt-flakes are falling, the accountants are singing their carols, and in every house the children are leaving out tripwires and caltrops to delay the inevitable march of the merciless Father Taxmas.

Did you have a good time at Rezzed? I didn’t go – humans, right? – but that’s fine because we clever ones, we get all the good footage without even leaving our tunnels. And because I showed up for the mixer anyway. They can’t stop me. Unknown Pleasures has spies everywhere.

It’s an even wider selection of obscurities for you today, as Unknown Pleasures brings you the best unsung indie games on Steam once more. Confusing RPS staffers by saying their own names to them this week: Groundhog crimes, Bushido yo-yos, and robotic wanderers.

notes.title: RICO kicks open the door and slides into stores
notes.content:
RICO is not a game that beats around the bush. It’s a roguelike-ish shooter built for co-op that sells that 80s hollywood buddy cop fantasy of punting open doors and clearing out waves of expendable mooks as you work your way up to whatever generic drug kingpin is behind it all. Out now and developed by Ground Shatter, I’ve played a few rounds of the game, and while it feels surprisingly bare-bones in places, there’s something to be said for its fast, two-player co-op focus.
